question: What is the normal resting respiratory rate for a healthy adult?
explanation: A normal, healthy adult at rest breathes between 12 and 20 times every minute. Rates outside this range can indicate underlying respiratory or metabolic problems. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why is cyanosis considered a poor early indicator of hypoxia?

options.A: It only appears after severe oxygen shortage has already developed
options.B: It is easily confused with normal pigmentation changes in the skin
options.C: It disappears completely when the patient stands up
options.D: It only occurs when the patient is holding their breath

explanation: Cyanosis is a late sign of low oxygen in the blood. Restlessness and confusion show up much earlier, so nurses must not wait for blue skin to give oxygen. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of the huff coughing technique?

options.A: To measure the total lung capacity of the patient
options.B: To force air deeply into closed alveoli sacs
options.C: To prevent the tongue from blocking the throat
options.D: To move mucus upward without collapsing the airways

explanation: Huff coughing keeps the vocal cords open while the patient exhales sharply, helping push mucus up from the lower airways safely. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h2)

question: A patient with thick lung secretions refuses to drink water because of nausea. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Force the patient to drink a full cup of water immediately
options.B: Report the fluid refusal and suggest IV hydration or anti-nausea medication
options.C: Document that the patient refuses care and leave the room
options.D: Stop all respiratory treatments until the nausea goes away on its own

explanation: Good hydration thins out thick mucus so it can be cleared easily. Addressing nausea and providing fluids through alternative routes helps maintain airway clearance. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h2)

question: Which oxygen delivery device provides the most precise and controlled oxygen concentration?
explanation: The Venturi mask uses interchangeable adapters to mix exact amounts of room air with oxygen, delivering a very specific percentage of gas. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h3)

question: Why must nurses enforce strict fire safety rules around patients receiving oxygen therapy?

options.A: Oxygen strongly supports combustion and makes fires spread much faster
options.B: Electrical equipment creates sparks that turn oxygen into a liquid
options.C: Patients on oxygen are more likely to fall asleep while smoking
options.D: Oxygen tanks will automatically explode if they touch plastic

explanation: While oxygen itself does not burn, it feeds fires vigorously, turning small sparks into dangerous blazes instantly. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h3)

question: When a patient needs both a bronchodilator and an inhaled corticosteroid, why should the bronchodilator be used first?

options.A: It stops the side effects of the steroid from harming the heart
options.B: It neutralizes stomach acid that might interfere with breathing
options.C: It opens the airways so the steroid can reach deeper into the lungs
options.D: It cleans the mouth so the patient does not develop a fungal infection

explanation: Using the bronchodilator first widens the bronchial tubes, allowing the corticosteroid to penetrate further down into the respiratory tree. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h4)

question: A patient is prescribed a metered-dose inhaler without a spacer and complains that the medicine just hits their throat. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Instruct the patient to hold their breath for five minutes after inhaling
options.B: Call the doctor to change the prescription to a skin patch
options.C: Advise the patient to obtain and use a spacer device to improve drug delivery
options.D: Tell the patient to swallow the medicine instead of breathing it in

explanation: Spacers act as a holding chamber that slows down the spray, preventing medication from depositing in the mouth and throat instead of the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h4)

question: What is the best initial position for a patient experiencing acute respiratory distress?
explanation: Sitting upright in high Fowler's position allows gravity to lower the diaphragm, giving the lungs maximum room to expand and making breathing easier. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h5)

question: How does pursed-lip breathing help a patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease?

options.A: It forces extra oxygen directly into the bloodstream through the mouth
options.B: It relaxes the stomach muscles to improve digestion
options.C: It stops the patient from coughing up thick mucus plugs
options.D: It slows down exhalation and keeps airways open longer

explanation: Pursed-lip breathing creates back-pressure in the airways, preventing them from collapsing too early and helping trap less air in the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h5)
